correctness.rationale: Positive weights ensure the polar partial isometry remains the forward shift. Pascal recurrence proves the exact binomial iterate. On the central binomial event, Taylor remainder has expected size O(n^{beta-1}), with exponential tail control; centered-binomial characteristic function is exactly cos(t/2)^n. Its Gaussian exponent has sharp critical value theta^2/16. Dense-support extension gives SOT convergence above 1/2; two limiting phase subsequences exclude even WOT below or at 1/2. Arbitrarily far tail windows approach a constant extremal phase, establishing the all-n norm equalities, while the diagonal self-commutator and the oscillatory integral estimate prove compactness and Cesàro mean 1. Standard-library checker passed 387 finite assertions; those do not establish the infinite-dimensional claim.

value.rationale: Motivated by asymptotic stability of a classical nonlinear operator transform, the same natural essentially normal positive-weighted-shift family with Cesàro mean 1 and vanishing weight increments exhibits three sharp operator-topology regimes. The boundary damping e^{-theta^2/16} and persistent exact norm gap epsilon demonstrate why mean-ergodic heuristics fail and identify a precise Gaussian local-frequency threshold. This is structural operator information, not an arbitrary single finite instance.
